Can you explain the main options in simple terms?

Here's a simple rundown of the main options:



Roller Blinds – one flat piece of fabric that rolls up and down. Affordable, easy to clean, and available in waterproof fabrics, so they're great for kitchens and bathrooms 


Roman Blinds – soft fabric that folds into neat pleats when raised. Cosy and stylish, with light filtering, blackout, or thermal linings 


Vertical Blinds – tall fabric louvres that rotate to tilt light and stack to one side. Ideal for large windows and patio doors 


Venetian Blinds – horizontal slats (usually aluminium or wood) you can tilt for precise light control, though they're not blackout 


Stick On / No Drill blinds – versions of the above that attach without drilling, including stick on roller, Roman, Venetian, and even shutters

How do I use it properly the very first time?

Using a roller blind the first time is really simple. Most use a beaded side chain: pull it one way and the blind rolls up, pull the other way and it lowers. A clutch inside the mechanism holds it securely at whatever height you leave it, so you can stop it anywhere you like 
.

If yours is a Soft Raise version, you just pull the blind down to the height you want, and a gentle push up on the bottom makes it glide back to the top. There's also a weighted bar along the bottom to keep the fabric hanging straight and neat. Just fit the child safety clip for the chain if it's included, and you're all set.
